title: Implementation of the Bio-Inspired Metaheuristic Firefly Algorithm (FA) Applied to Maximum Power Point Tracking of Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: In this paper, an algorithm for the maximum extraction of energy generated by photovoltaic (PV) systems was presented. The tracking of the global maximum point of the system is complex due to the non-linearity of the current-voltage (I-V) characteristic curve of the photovoltaic modules, as they vary according to the temperature and solar irradiation in the module. To obtain the best energy efficiency in these systems, it is important that the generation is delivering the maximum power available through the arrangement. In order to solve such problems, in this work an efficient MPPT-FA method was proposed, which showed good traceability when compared to traditional methods. Most traditional MPPT techniques are not able to find the global maximum point to extract the maximum power provided by the PV system. Finally, the Firefly Metaheuristic MPPT method proved to be robust against several partial shading scenarios. Simulations were presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposal when compared to the traditional MPPT-PO method.

title: Eagle-PSO: A Bio-Inspired Algorithm for Maximum Power Point Tracking with Precision Control in Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is critical for maximizing energy yield of photovoltaic (PV) systems. Nonlinearity and dynamic conditions challenge conventional tracking algorithms. Bio‑inspired methods like Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) improve performance but suffer from premature convergence and insufficient precision control. Traditional algorithms (P&O, INC) degrade under partial shading, while standard PSO lacks controlled precision and adaptive exploration‑exploitation balance. This work builds on a recent practical study where a passive cooling system with PSO‑MPPT was validated on a 30 W PV module in Tunisia, providing baseline performance of 95.7% tracking accuracy and 0.017 W mean absolute error. To improve upon these results, we introduce Eagle‑PSO MPPT, a novel hybrid algorithm inspired by eagle hunting. It integrates three innovations: (1) a precision control system with tunable error target, (2) a multi‑resolution vision mechanism using enhanced interpolation, and (3) a hierarchical hunting strategy. Validated on the same experimental dataset, Eagle‑PSO achieves a final tracking precision of 0.004 W (76.3% improvement), reduces convergence time by 42.8%, and reaches 99.2% efficiency under STC. Under complex partial shading, success rate in locating the global maximum is 94% (vs. 59% for standard PSO). These figures significantly enhance prior art. Eagle‑PSO effectively addresses core limitations of existing bio‑inspired MPPT methods. Its precision‑oriented approach improves energy yield and economic return. Future work includes parameter self‑adaptation and hardware implementation.

title: BIO-INSPIRED OPTIMIZATION FOR ENHANCED MAXIMUM POWER POINT TRACKING IN GRID-CONNECTED PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEMS
